user.title: UniFi LTE device
user.description: Home Assistant logs in to the device over SSH and talks to the LTE modem directly. Use the device SSH credentials from the UniFi Network app (Settings → System → Advanced → Device Authentication). Enter a password, a private key, or both.

data_description.host: IP address of the LTE device. A fixed IP is not required: Home Assistant follows IP changes via DHCP discovery.
data_description.private_key: Optional. Paste the whole key including the BEGIN/END lines. Keys with a passphrase are not supported.

host_key.title: Confirm host key
host_key.description:
{host} presented this {key_type} host key:

`{fingerprint}`

If you want to check it: `ssh-keygen -lf /etc/dropbear/dropbear_rsa_host_key` on the device, or the fingerprint your SSH client shows. Home Assistant only connects to the device while it presents exactly this key.

reauth_confirm.title: Re-authenticate
reauth_confirm.description:
The connection to {host} was rejected. Usually the host key changed after a firmware update or factory reset.

Stored key: `{old_fingerprint}`
Current key: `{new_fingerprint}`

Submit to trust the current key. Leave password and key empty to keep the stored credentials.

reconfigure.title: Reconfigure
reconfigure.description: Leave password and key empty to keep the stored credentials.

error.cannot_connect: Cannot connect to the device via SSH.
error.invalid_auth: Login rejected. Check username, password and key.
error.no_credentials: Enter a password or a private key.
error.host_key_changed: The host key changed during setup. Try again.
error.modem_error: Logged in, but the LTE modem did not respond (AT port missing or busy). Is this a UniFi LTE device?

abort.no_mac: The device did not report a MAC address. Is this a UniFi LTE device?

data.delete_after_receive: Delete received SMS from the SIM

data_description.scan_interval: How often the SIM is checked for new SMS (signal values are updated with it).
data_description.delete_after_receive: The SIM holds only about 20 messages. Without deleting, new SMS are rejected once it is full.
data_description.default_recipients: Recipients of the notify entity (international format, e.g. +491701234567).
data_description.accept_host_key_change: Some firmware versions create a new SSH host key on every reboot. If enabled, Home Assistant trusts the new key, keeps working and reports it under Repairs. Only enable this if you use key login: with a password, a device impersonating the LTE device on your network would receive the password.

send_sms.name: Send SMS
send_sms.description: Sends an SMS via the LTE modem. Long texts are split into up to 10 parts; texts with characters outside the GSM alphabet (e.g. emoji) are sent as Unicode with fewer characters per part.

config_entry_id.name: Device
config_entry_id.description: Only needed if more than one LTE device is set up.

recipients.name: Recipients
recipients.description: Phone numbers, preferably in international format (+49…).

entry_not_found.message: No UniFi LTE SMS entry with ID {entry_id}.

entry_required.message: More than one UniFi LTE device is set up. Select one.

no_entry.message: No UniFi LTE device is set up and loaded.

message_too_long.message: The message needs {parts} SMS parts, the maximum is 10.

no_default_recipients.message: No default recipients set. Add them in the integration options or use the action ulte_sms.send_sms.

host_key_accepted.title: Host key of {title} changed
host_key_accepted.description:
The SSH host key of {host} changed at {time} and was accepted automatically (option enabled).

Old: `{old}`
New: `{new}`

This is expected after a reboot or firmware update of the device. If the device did not restart, check your network. Dismiss this message once checked.
